**Grant Application: Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC)**

To the Sacramento Stockton Blvd Grant Committee,

Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC), a minority-owned social enterprise, addresses a critical and often overlooked need: gun safety education within Sacramento's communities of color. These communities are disproportionately affected by gun violence and accidental firearm injuries, necessitating culturally competent and accessible preventative education.

Our innovative programs deliver vital information where it's most needed. We engage youth through our "Gloxsie 21" cartoon IP, delivering crucial safety lessons through relatable storytelling. Concurrently, we equip young adults with vital AI literacy, fostering economic opportunity alongside responsible citizenship. Our hands-on community workshops, conducted in partnership with the respected Church of Legacy, provide essential gun storage, handling, and conflict resolution training for families.

This multi-faceted approach yields measurable outcomes: reduced accidental firearm injuries, increased responsible gun storage practices, enhanced digital literacy, and safer communities. As a minority-owned organization deeply embedded in the neighborhoods we serve, GAFC brings unique trust and understanding. Our partnership with Church of Legacy further grounds our work, providing established community access.

A $15,000 grant from the Sacramento Stockton Blvd Fund would directly support curriculum development, workshop materials, and outreach efforts for these vital programs. This investment will empower GAFC to expand our reach, ensuring more Sacramento families have the knowledge and tools to prevent tragic accidents and foster a safer environment for our children. We are uniquely qualified to make a lasting, positive impact.
